condition.notes: Rail voltage is ABOVE the typical tolerance max. This is dangerous — overvoltage can damage downstream ICs. Power off immediately. A high rail is by definition not a short. Common causes: feedback divider open (high-side resistor), low-side FET open (synchronous buck runs unregulated), OVP circuit failed.

next_steps.action: DANGER: rail voltage is HIGH. Power off immediately to prevent downstream damage. Do NOT re-apply power until the cause is identified. With power off, measure the feedback divider resistors and check the low-side FET for open-circuit.

measure.what: Feedback divider resistor values + low-side FET drain-source resistance
measure.where: FB pin divider resistors; low-side FET (synchronous bucks only)
measure.expected: FB divider values per the schematic/service manual. Low-side FET drain-source should read low ohms (RDS_on) gate-off, high impedance gate-on; a FET that reads open in both directions is failed-open.
measure.safety: UNPOWERED. Discharge all caps before measuring resistance. Overvoltage may have already damaged downstream ICs — inspect for bulged/vented caps and charred ICs before re-applying power.

interpretations.then: Feedback divider is open. The regulator sees FB pin too low and drives the output high to compensate. Replace the open resistor with the correct value. WARNING: downstream ICs may already be damaged from the overvoltage — verify them before re-applying power.
Low-side FET failed open. The buck cannot freewheel, so the output rises unregulated. Replace the low-side FET. Verify the gate driver survived.

interpretations.if_result: FB divider and FETs both good
interpretations.then: Cause unclear. Suspect the controller IC itself (internal reference or error amp drift). Replace the controller. Do NOT re-apply power without a current-limited supply to limit damage if the fault recurs.
